name: Logic Grid Engine
description: Generates a puzzle, validates a solution, and refuses to ship either without checking that exactly one answer exists. Uniqueness is the whole contract: a sudoku with two solutions is not a hard sudoku, it is a broken one, and a player who deduces correctly and is marked wrong has been lied to by the generator. So generation runs a solver twice — once to find a solution, once to prove there is no second — and a candidate that fails is discarded rather than published. The engine is rule-set agnostic: sudoku, nonogram and kakuro differ in their constraint functions, not in this loop, which is why the constraints are an input and the search is not.

inputs.name: ruleSet
inputs.description: Constraint family: sudoku, nonogram, kakuro or a declared custom set.

inputs.name: targetClues
inputs.description: Givens left after carving. Fewer is harder, and the uniqueness check is what stops 'fewer' becoming 'ambiguous'.

inputs.name: requireUniqueSolution
inputs.description: Whether a generated puzzle must be proven to have exactly one answer. Turning this off is how a generator starts lying to players.

outputs.name: puzzle
outputs.description: The generated grid with its givens.

outputs.name: solution
outputs.description: The unique answer, held for validation.

outputs.name: uniquenessProven
outputs.description: Whether the second solve confirmed no alternative.
